original_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface in characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b(X) such that every reduced irreducible curve C subset X satisfies C^2 >= -b(X)?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s main bounded-negativity conjecture in the ambient object (a smooth projective surface), the characteristic-zero restriction, the existence of a constant depending only on X, and the universal quantifier over reduced irreducible curves C on X.
missing_details: The paper states the bound with a strict inequality, namely C^2 > -b(X), not the weak inequality C^2 >= -b(X).
For a stand-alone formulation, b(X) should be said to depend only on the fixed surface X.
For full self-containment, C^2 should be identified as the self-intersection number of C on X.
The paper keeps the scope exactly to reduced, irreducible curves; reducible curves are treated separately later in Section 3.8, so the question should not be broadened.
The characteristic-zero hypothesis should be retained exactly, since the nearby discussion explains that it is essential in general by giving a positive-characteristic counterexample.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface over a field of characteristic zero. Does there exist a positive constant b(X), depending only on X, such that for every reduced, irreducible curve C contained in X, the self-intersection number of C satisfies C^2 > -b(X)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the full Bounded Negativity Conjecture, not the weaker genus-parameterized variants, because it asks for one lower bound that works for all reduced irreducible curves on a fixed surface X. In this paper that statement appears exactly as Conjecture 3.3.1 in Section 3.3. The only substantive correction needed is to use the paper’s strict inequality C^2 > -b(X). The nearby context also shows why the characteristic-zero hypothesis must be preserved, and why the question should remain restricted to irreducible curves: Example 3.3.3 gives the positive-characteristic obstruction, while Section 3.8 introduces reducible bounded negativity as a separate conjecture. Proposition 3.3.2 confirms the intended notation and form of the conjecture by proving it in the special case where -mK_X is effective.
